To: page:wensum-valley-hospice-bookshop
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Light Up a Life 2026

Yes, Hilary, we are doing the tree again this year, and I'm so glad you're bringing your sister. A few of you have asked, so here is everything in one place.

Memory tags will be in the shop from Monday 16 November. The suggested donation is £3. If you would rather write your tag somewhere quieter than a busy bookshop, there are envelopes on the counter so you can take one home and bring it back when you're ready. The tree goes into the window on Saturday 28 November, and we'll switch the lights on that afternoon at 4pm. The Gildencroft Primary choir are kindly coming back to sing three or four carols, and Doreen has promised mince pies again. Last year they didn't survive the first carol, so you may want to stand near the front.

Every name on the tree will be read aloud at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm, in the day centre. You are very welcome to come, but you don't have to be there for your name to be read. It will be read all the same.

I'd like to say something a little more personal this year, if you'll let me. My husband Ray died at the hospice in November 2019, so it is seven years this month. The first year I hung his tag I could hardly write it. My hand wouldn't do what I asked, and I think it took me most of an afternoon to manage his name. Now I write it at the counter, with the same pen, in between serving people and answering questions about railway timetables. It doesn't get easier exactly. It changes, though, and the tree has been part of that for me.

I mention it only because I know some of you are in that first year now, or the second, or the twentieth. There's no right way to do this. The tree isn't only for hospice families, either. It's for anyone who is missing someone, whoever they were and however you lost them.

Please also know that you don't need to buy anything or fill in anything. If you just want to come and stand by the tree for a few minutes, you are welcome to do that, as often as you like. Some people come in, look for a name, and leave again without a word, and that's perfectly all right. We'll leave you be, or put the kettle on, whichever seems wanted.

Thank you to everyone who remembered with us last year. By the end the tree carried 412 names, and I read a good many of them while I was dusting the window display. I hope you know how much it meant to the people at the hospice, and to us in the shop, to see it so full. What you gave went straight back into care, including the night sitters who sit with families through the long hours, and I can't think of anything better for it to do.

So do come in from the 16th, or come on the 28th for the lights and the singing, or just come and stand by the tree when you need to. It will be lit until Twelfth Night.

With love,
Jean
